independence_declaration.statement: qa-verifier authored no product implementation in the DG3 scope. In this round I wrote only QA tests and evidence: the spec docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/qa/tests/round-5/e2e/dg3-qa-r5.spec.ts (outside the frozen candidate), the evidence under docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG3/qa/round-5/, this record and its narrative. Every result comes from my own runs in two disposable clones of 21e2742 under $TMPDIR, both removed at the end: review-dg3 for all suites, and probe-dg3 for the throwaway mutation probes only. HEAD was 40c84e8 at the start and 40b422e at the end. Every intermediate commit came from other reviewers' auto-committed evidence or an orchestrator assignment, and touched only docs/delivery/. The candidate ID recomputes identical in the working tree at the start and end, at --ref 21e2742 and --ref HEAD, and in the clone (757 files). I did not open any other reviewer's round-5 record or evidence, nor the new orchestrator assignment, and I formed my verdict from my own runs. Product gates G1-G6 are business approvals inside the product and never imply DG0-DG7. Every business decision in my tests is a synthetic demo record that approves nothing real.

checks_run.procedure: T-DG3-KBE-G from the acceptance side: the EvalError-rethrow rule is enforced by lint and by the source scan. In the throwaway probe clone I appended 17 forbidden handler forms plus 1 allowed shape to packages/shared/src/formula/parse.ts, and separately to packages/shared/src/value.ts. Each time I ran ESLint and the fuzz.test.ts source scan, then restored the file. The forms are W1 catch {}, W2 finally { return }, W4 Promise.then.catch, W5 a wrapping catch, a differently named parameter, else, a statement before the rethrow, a rethrow of another class, finally { break }, finally { throw }, a shadowing const EvalError, async/await, queueMicrotask, ["then"]/?.catch/.finally, an async arrow, a braced rethrow and a negated rethrow. I also appended 3 edge forms outside the documented denylist: a finally that calls a throwing helper, `using` with a throwing dispose, and a generator finally.
checks_run.command: npx eslint <file>; npx vitest run --project unit-node packages/shared/src/formula/fuzz.test.ts -t 'source scan' (mutated, then restored)
checks_run.environment: probe clone probe-dg3 @21e2742; node v24.21.0; ESLint 10.1.0
checks_run.expected: every forbidden form is refused by lint and by the scan (non-zero exit), and the allowed shape is not reported; after the restore, lint exits 0 and git status is clean
checks_run.actual: EXIT 1 by design for the 17 forms. ESLint reports 26 errors per file on exactly 17 distinct lines (254-270 in parse.ts, 299-315 in value.ts), one per forbidden form, and nothing on the allowed shape. The scan test fails with exactly the hits Promise, async, await, .then/.catch/.finally, 'catch without EvalError rethrow', 'finally with return/throw/break/continue' and 'EvalError outside instanceof', in both files. The 3 edge forms pass both static layers (lint EXIT 0, scan passes). That is consistent with ADR-0024 §6, which calls these layers a best-effort denylist; QA-R5-01c shows that the run-time layer refuses them. After the restore: git status clean, and eslint on formula/ and value.ts gives EXIT 0.

checks_run.procedure: From the acceptance side, an exercised string code generation inside the try of each of the 4 catch sites must fail the no-codegen invocation as EvalError. The sites are validateFormula, the evaluateAst walk, formatDecimal and parseFormula, which is new in round 5. The mutation is a Function-constructor call through a key assembled at run time. As an edge probe I then wrap the same generation so that the EvalError is replaced in flight: by a finally that throws while an exception is in flight (E1, E2, E4) or by a `using` dispose that throws (E3). The first edge attempt in 01c used an unconditional thrower; it was inconclusive and was repeated in 01c2.
checks_run.command: per mutation: npx vitest run --project unit-node packages/shared/src/formula packages/shared/src/value.test.ts; npx vitest run --project unit-formula-nocodegen; git checkout -- <file>
checks_run.expected: each mutation makes unit-formula-nocodegen exit non-zero and the normal process pass; M1-M4 surface EvalError, with no 'could not be processed' problem; after the restore, nocodegen exits 0
checks_run.actual: M1: nocodegen EXIT 1, 73 failed. M2: EXIT 1, 24 failed. M3: EXIT 1, 4 failed. M4 (parseFormula): EXIT 1, 103 failed. Each fails with 'EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed', with 0 'could not be processed' lines, and the normal process exits 0 for every mutation. 01c2 edge forms: the normal process passes 240/240 each time, and nocodegen fails E1 24, E2 5, E3 73 and E4 104. The replaced error surfaces as an 'internal' problem (SuppressedError or RangeError) or as a null display, and the internal-failure rule and the outcome assertions refuse it. So the forms the static layers miss are still refused at run time on exercised paths. The first 01c E1-E4 block is inconclusive and superseded: its thrower was unconditional, so the normal process failed too (22, 7, 70 and 100 failed). It is disclosed in RUN-NOTES item 2. After every restore: git status clean, nocodegen EXIT 0 (220 passed, 1 skipped). The skip is fuzz.test.ts:457 it.skipIf(NOCODEGEN), the ESLint-config assertion, skipped because ESLint's ajv needs new Function. It runs and passes in unit-node.

summary: PASS, no new findings. The T-DG3-KBE-G repair holds from the acceptance side. Lint and the source scan refuse every one of 17 forbidden handler forms (W1, W2, W4, W5 and the other catch, finally, async and shadowing spellings) in both parse.ts and value.ts, and accept the allowed shape. An exercised code generation in each of the 4 catch sites, parseFormula included, fails the no-codegen invocation with EvalError. Three edge forms outside the documented best-effort static denylist (a finally that throws in flight, a `using` dispose that throws, a generator finally) are still refused at run time; this is an observation, not a finding.
